title: Complete Explanation of New Features in Patch 7.3: AI New Features Launched!
description: The CLO7.3 patch version introduction is here! Introducing brand new AI features: AI Texture Generator, Virtual Model Face Generator... and more feature upgrades. Come and get the latest updates first! CLO looks forward to your feedback!
transcript:
Now let's talk about the new features and functional optimizations of the 7.3 Pudding version, mainly explained in four aspects: main functions, 2D, materials, and rendering.

First, let's introduce the main functions. The first main function is the AI sticker generator.  
When creating a sticker, there is no need for manual editing. For example, you can enter keywords to remove the background.  
You can also preview the created sticker pattern on 3D clothing to ensure that the sticker pattern matches the 3D garment.  
Currently, the AI sticker generator can easily create stickers with embroidery, fashion, and wave art characteristics.  
The current AI sticker generator is a public version of the function. Future usage policies may change.  

Next, let's look at how to open the AI sticker generator.  
There are two ways here, corresponding to different application scenarios.  
First, if you want to create a new sticker pattern, click on the sticker in the Object window. Then click on the magic wand icon above, which is the AI sticker generator.  
The second way is: if you want to use the AI sticker generator on a sticker that has already been added, select the desired sticker. Then click on the Attribute Editor, next to the default parameters, click on the AI sticker generator.  

Now let's look at the AI sticker generator interface.  
First, the Pattern Type option.  
In Pattern Type, you can create a sticker pattern closer to your desired style.  
After selecting the Pattern Type, choose the art style from the drop-down menu.  
Currently, there are three styles: embroidery, fashion, and wave art.  
If you want to create a sticker not limited by any pattern type and only created by AI prompts, select Pattern Type 5.  
If you want to create a sticker with a transparent background, select the transparent background option.  

Next is the Keyword Prompt.  
Enter the keyword describing the pattern you want to create in the Keyword Prompt box.  
The AI sticker preview will appear at the bottom after creation.  
If you click on the History Record option on the right, it will display previous creations.  
Additionally, you can check the options and keywords used for each sticker creation.  
Note that the history record is retained only until the cloud software is closed.  

Next, let's review the function usage process.  
Pattern Type is not an exception.  
We will create an AI sticker by entering a keyword.  
In the Keyword Prompt box, enter the keyword describing the image you want to generate.  

Here are some tips for entering keywords:  
- The AI sticker generator supports languages from more than 50 countries. You can use any language provided by the cloud.  
- It is recommended to enter keywords in English because English prompts tend to be more precise.  
- Enter single words rather than long descriptive sentences, as long sentences may distort the image.  
- Separate keywords with dots or spaces. Using spaces increases the number of keywords.  
After entering the keywords, click the Create button to generate a sticker.  
During creation, you can see the current server link and progress.  
If there are many users in the queue, the wait time may be longer. In this case, you can minimize the window using the arrow button in the upper right corner.  
Once the sticker is created, a text prompt will appear to indicate completion.  
After creation, click the Apply button. The created image will be added to the Object window and applied as a sticker.  

To check the effect of an existing sticker on a garment, select it in the Object window first, then drag it to the desired position on the 3D garment. You can easily check if it suits the garment.  

Next, let's take embroidery as an example.  
Select the art style in Pattern Type.  
Choose Embroidery from the drop-down menu.  
Select Transparent Background.  
Create an embroidery sticker with a transparent background.  
Enter the keyword and click Create.  
You can apply the created sticker to the 3D garment immediately by clicking Apply. You can see the sticker effect.  

To generate as many diversified images as possible, even with the same prompt, the AI sticker generator produces different results each time.  
If you want to update the prompt while keeping characteristics of the previous result, click the True icon.  
Hovering the mouse over the True icon will display its tooltip: "Keep the prompt result to generate similar results."  
Clicking the True icon generates a new image similar to the previously generated one.  
Note: The generated image may vary depending on prompt additions or modifications.  

If you want to generate a new image randomly, click the Random button. Pattern type and keywords will be randomly selected.  
Using the AI sticker generator, you can easily create the stickers you want.  

Now let's introduce the second main function: the virtual model face generator.  
This function is developed in cooperation with NOVA. Its main feature is the ability to modify the existing close-up image of a virtual model.  
It can change the face of an existing close-up virtual model, not only altering the texture but also using AI-generated facial images or uploading specific facial image files to modify the virtual model's facial grid structure.  
The converted virtual model follows a unique close-up virtual model format and can be used immediately.  
It can also be applied to various virtual models provided by the TuKu window and Connect platform.  

For AI-based facial image generation, users can select the desired gender, age range, and race as presets and input keywords describing relevant features for generation.  
Alternatively, users can upload a specific facial image file for generation.  
Simply select the image upload collection that meets the requirements.  

Now let's look at the usage process.  
First, run the virtual model. There are two ways to activate this function:  
1. Use the Virtual Model Human Generator under the Virtual Model menu in the top main menu bar.  
2. Select the virtual model, then use the Virtual Model Human Generator tool in the Body Model box within the Attribute Editor.  

Next, the virtual model human generator window interface.  
At the top, choose between the Prompt option and Picture option.  
The Prompt option allows you to create and convert images based on AI, while the Picture option enables uploading specific image files for the face.  

Let's use the Prompt option first.  
In the top menu bar, select the required face gender, age group, and race.  
The gender option is automatically set based on the selected virtual model's gender.  
Currently, this function applies only to female virtual models, but gender options will expand in future versions.  
The age option presets the age range of the face to create, currently from 10 to 80 years old.  
The race option presets the race of the face to create. Available options are Asian, Caucasian, African, Middle Eastern, and Latin American.  

In the Keyword Prompt window, enter the keywords describing the desired facial features.  
At the bottom AI face gender section, you can preview AI-generated facial images.  
To revisit previously created virtual model images, click the History Record option on the right.  
This opens a window showing the facial image, creation options, and hints used.  
Note that history records are saved only until the CLO software is closed.  

Now, for the image options:  
Through the top image menu, select the gender of the virtual model for conversion.  
Click the Upload button in the Picture window to upload a specific image file for face conversion.  
To revisit uploaded images, click the History Record option.  
History is retained only until the CLO software is closed.  

Next, let's operate the function.  
Set options, enter keyword prompts, and generate.  
Now, create a human face image based on AI technology.  
First, select the age and race of the desired face.  
In the text prompt section, enter descriptive text about the facial features.  
This function supports about 50 languages, all provided by CLO, but English input is recommended for higher accuracy.  
After entering the prompt, click the Start button to generate the image.  

To improve the quality of the generated virtual model face, refer to the reference image shown in the AI human face checkbox.  
It is recommended to check before generating that the created image clearly shows the face without hair or shadows covering it.  
After understanding these suggestions, click Start to generate the image.  

While generating, you can monitor server connection progress and queue position.  
After generation, click the Switch button.  
The CLO virtual model's face will change according to the generated image.  
The body texture and color of the virtual model will also adjust to maintain natural coordination with the face color.  

If you need ideas or help with facial features after setting gender, age, and race, click the Random icon shaped like a brush.  
This randomly enters a hint describing a human face.  
Even with the same hint, AI-generated faces will vary.  

If you want to create different facial images or update the hint while maintaining the original result, click the True icon.  
Hovering the mouse over the True icon shows a tooltip explaining it keeps keywords to generate similar results.  
Clicking it generates a new image similar to the previous one.  
You can update the hint and generate a new image while preserving similarity.  
Note that new results may vary depending on additions or modifications to the hint.  

If many users generate faces simultaneously, creation time may increase.  
During waiting, you can perform other tasks.  
If the wait is long, click the arrow button in the upper right corner to minimize the window.  
After generation completes, a progress prompt will appear for effective use.  

Finally, some tips for inputting hint keywords to create desired facial images:  
- Enter single words instead of long descriptive sentences for more effective results.  
- Use two numbers (likely meaning separators) to divide words to prevent image distortion.  
- To emphasize a specific word, enclose it in square brackets. This adds weight and influence to the word.  

Next, let's convert the virtual model's face by uploading a specific image.  
First, ensure the virtual model's gender is correctly set.  
Click the Upload button to select a specific face image file.  
To generate high-quality virtual faces, refer to the image shown in the image viewfinder as a reference.  
Recommended images should clearly show facial features without hair or shadows covering the face.  

After uploading, click Convert.  
The virtual model's face will change according to the uploaded image.  
Body texture and color will adjust for natural coordination with the face tone.  

Previously, creating realistic and diversified virtual models required substantial effort.  
Now, with the virtual face generator, you can easily and quickly create lifelike virtual models.  
The AI face generator is currently a public version. Future usage policies may change.  

Next, we discuss the 2D floating version functions.  

First, the 2D CAD continuous editing optimization.  
Improving continuous editing increases work efficiency.  

Let's look at the function's optimization points.  
In previous versions, checking if panels were linked required using the editing panel tool and focusing on a single-frame section.  
From this floating version, you can use the Display Link option in the menu bar at the upper left of the 2D panel window to show or hide linked line diagrams and check whether multiple lines are linked.  

Additionally, before the floating version, removing a link required right-clicking to set the linked line, then selecting the editing link tool to remove the link.  
For floating lines, you needed to select Edit Floating Line, then right-click the linked line to remove the link.  
From this version, to improve workflow, after selecting the Edit Panel tool, you can also select the linked line and right-click to remove the link.  

There are two more functions to introduce together.  
Previously, after setting a linked line, adjusting the length or proportion of the linked line did not change the length of the linked line to match the edited line's size, though the linked state remained.  
This has been improved.  
After setting a linked line, adjusting the line length or panel proportion will also modify the linked line accordingly.  

Next, let's demonstrate how to use these improvements.  
Use the Edit Panel tool to select the linked line panel, then adjust its size.  
You will see the linked line modify together.  

When using the Edit Point or Line tool to move or rotate the line, the length of the linked line remains unchanged, but the length of other lines changes.  
Similarly, using the Edit Panel tool to select and drag the linked line or points on the line works the same.  

When using the Edit Panel tool, right-click and enter a distance value in the output window; the linked line maintains its size value and changes accordingly.  
When adjusting line size with keyboard arrow keys on points, the same applies.  

Finally, if you select both ends of a linked line simultaneously and right-click, you can use the Array tool to modify the end point positions.  
The array works similarly for both ends of the linked line.  

Using the optimized linked edit function can better improve work efficiency.  

Next, the improved 2D panel selection efficiency.  
After this improvement, you can press shortcut keys and select necessary lines or panels more easily.  

To check this, open a project file with multiple inner lines.  
Previously, with many inner lines and shapes, you had to select some inner lines first and then deselect unnecessary parts.  
Now you can select desired parts easily.  

For example, to select folds in a skirt:  
Select the Edit Panel tool in the 2D toolbar.  
Hold the CTRL key and click with the left mouse button to select the inner lines you want.  
All lines in the dragged area will be selected.  

Besides inner lines, you can select entire panels by selecting part of the panel.  
After selecting the Edit Panel tool, hold CTRL, left-click and drag to select a portion of the panel.  
All panels in the dragged area will be selected.  

You can easily select inner lines and panels by pressing CTRL during selection.  

Next feature: 2D Edit Panel measurement angle.  
A new feature allows checking the angle of a panel outline or the angle between overlapping lines.  
This makes it easy to check angles at specific positions during panel creation or modification.  

For example, to check the angle at the end of two panels:  
Select the Edit Panel tool in the 2D toolbar.  
Select the panel end point to check the angle.  
Right-click and select the endpoint option to display the angle at this point.  
The panel shape will change according to the angle between the two panel ends.  
You can check and modify the angle to the desired shape.  

You can also open the 2D Edit Panel to display line length or angle functions.  
All panel angles can be checked, including the angle between overlapping lines in a pocket.  
Angles can be adjusted dynamically as lines move.  
This function facilitates checking angles at special panel positions.  

Next, seam allowance optimization.  

First, seam allowance at panel corners.  
Previously, when seam allowance was added at a panel corner extension, repeated seam allowances could be created.  
This caused seam allowance measurements to mismatch actual cutting needs, leading to inaccurate sewing information.  

To address this, two options are provided for seam allowance positioning within seam allowance:  
Use the Cut tool to select the cut.  
In the Attribute Editor, the Cut menu differs for corner cuts and seam allowance cuts.  
When selecting corner cut, a new Cut Position menu appears, allowing you to choose duplicating the cut to the extension point or to the center position.  
Choosing Extension Point shows the cut from the panel cut level to the vertical extension point.  
Choosing Center Position displays the cut at the corner extension as before.  
This improvement provides more accurate panel information.  

Another seam allowance optimization: supporting seam allowance addition to hollows inside panels.  
Previously, seam allowance could only be created from panel outlines.  
From the previous version, hollows are identified as outlines, enabling seam allowance creation for hollows.  
In the 2D window, select the Seam Allowance tool, then select the hollow position to create seam allowance.  
The hollow is identified as an outline, and seam allowance is created accordingly.  
This allows seam allowances to display inside hollows, enabling more diverse panel creation in CLO.  

Next, 2D paper pattern improvement.  
Previously, if a paper pattern created in 2D CAD was located far from the center, the paper pattern's position remained unchanged when imported into CLO.  
Thus, paper samples needed to be recreated at the 00 position for convenient location.  
From the latest version, when importing DXF files, the file is based on the 00 position and centered in the 2D window while maintaining all existing paper sample layers.  
The improved DXF import function improves work efficiency.  

Next, code selection improvement.  
In the updated version, the Object window's code display has been optimized.  
When opening and displaying codes in CLO, the color of code lines is displayed randomly.  
In the Object window code options, click the eye icon next to the color block to show or hide code lines of a specific size.  
You can click the color block to remove the color or modify the code line color.  
When creating a new code size, a color is randomly generated.  
You can also choose the color block after the size name to remove or select a color.  
Similarly, when opening and displaying code in CLO mode, different size boards display colors randomly, which can be modified by color blocks.  
This enables automatic or specified color assignments to identify paper samples with code lines or in hard disk mode.  

Next, introduction of the new hair function.  
First, a hair material has been added to compensation light, the Composite Energy option.  
When hair density is high, light may not penetrate between hair strands, causing rendering to appear darker than normal.  
Enabling this option corrects lost light, making hair brightness closer to real effects.  

Additionally, from the current version, CLO rendering supports V-Ray.  
First, apply the hair material to the board.  
Hair effects can only be viewed in the rendering window, so open rendering in V-Ray mode.  

Hair parameters now include length, thickness, density, curl, gravity, curve strength, curve direction, and initial direction.  
Currently, 8 hair patterns can be applied.  

Next, let's review application of new hair features.  
First is the curl pattern.  
Add a curl pattern to control the number and radius of curls.  
The curl pattern is a black-and-white hair pattern, where black means no curl and white means curl is applied.  

Second is the gravity pattern, also a black-and-white pattern, simulating hair gravity effects.  

Third is the curve intensity sticker, expressing hair curvature intensity.  
It is a black-and-white sticker where black means no curve and white means curve.  

Fourth is the curve direction sticker.  
It defines the hair's curve direction.  
The curve direction sticker is an RGB color sticker, determining texture direction by color.  
In practice, a hair spray image can show different hair curve directions.  

Fifth is the initial direction sticker, defining hair root direction (initial direction).  

Since the sticker suits hair plants, we can apply stickers in Substance Painter to CLO for more realistic hair creation.  

Next, rendering updates.  
From the new version, 360-degree panoramic landscape images can be rendered.  
Additionally, you can use rendering spaces created in CLO inside CLOSET to build virtual exhibition halls.  
First, import OBJ files into CLO, then move them to the center of the 360-degree landscape space.  
When rendering, create wall-mounted exhibition halls on all four sides.  
The 360-degree landscape image will appear more natural.  

Open the rendering window and click the camera attribute tool.  
The camera attribute window now has a Lens Type option.  
Click the download icon to see two options:  
- Default option (existing lens type)  
- Full lens option (new option)  

Click the Full Lens option.  
The field of view changes from 15° default to 60°.  
All models, scenes, and props in the 3D window display on a grid surface, making camera placement and V-Ray rendering easier.  

Next, set image size to the recommended size in the CLOSET production manual.  
The finished rendering image can be added to the Space button in Edit Mode as a new space for CLOSET virtual exhibitions.  

Next, rendering function optimization.  
Sometimes objects have wavy Moiré shadow problems when rendering.  
The updated version adds an Image Filter option.  
Adjusting this in V-Ray rendering solves Moiré problems.  

Open the rendering function.  
Click the rendering property icon in the toolbar.  
An Image Filter option is added at the bottom of the property editor window.  
The default Image Filter size is 1.5.  

Open synchronization rendering.  
You may see Moiré on clothing in the render window.  
The Image Filter size can be adjusted from 1 (minimum) to 10 (maximum).  
The larger the value, the less the Moiré shadow.  
Adjust the value and turn on synchronization rendering to see the effect.  

For example, with the previous value at 1 and filter at 1.5, Moiré may appear.  
Increasing to a higher value reduces Moiré significantly.  
After stopping rendering and re-enabling synchronization rendering, Moiré nearly disappears.  

This function effectively improves rendering image quality.  

If you recall, the scene had Moiré at the top left corner initially.  
Setting the Image Filter to maximum eliminated it.  
Reducing below 1.5 causes Moiré to reappear.  
Adjusting the filter value can control Moiré visibility.  

This completes the overview of new features and optimizations in the 7.3 Pudding version.

markdown_content: # Complete Explanation of New Features in Patch 7.3: AI New Features Launched! This document details the new features and functional optimizations introduced in the 7.3 Pudding version, focusing on four main areas: main functions, 2D improvements, materials, and rendering updates. --- ## Main Functions Overview This section covers the two primary new AI-powered functions: the AI sticker generator and the virtual model face generator. It explains their capabilities, interfaces, usage procedures, and important settings for generating stickers and virtual faces with AI assistance. ### AI Sticker Generator The AI sticker generator automates sticker creation without manual editing, enabling users to generate sticker patterns using keyword prompts. It supports previewing stickers on 3D garments to ensure proper fit. - **Supported Styles:** Embroidery, fashion, and wave art. - **Background Options:** Transparent background selectable. - **Current Status:** Public version; future usage policies may change. #### How to Access Two methods are available depending on the scenario: 1. **Creating a New Sticker:** - Click on the sticker in the Object window. - Click the magic wand icon (AI sticker generator) above. 2. **Modifying an Existing Sticker:** - Select the sticker. - In the Attribute Editor, next to default parameters, click the AI sticker generator. #### Interface and Features - **Pattern Type:** Choose from embroidery, fashion, wave art, or select Pattern Type 5 to generate stickers solely from AI prompts without style constraints. - **Transparent Background:** Option to generate stickers with transparent backgrounds. - **Keyword Prompt:** Enter keywords describing the desired pattern. - **History Record:** Displays previous creations and their used keywords; resets when cloud software closes. #### Usage Guidelines - Supports over 50 languages; English is recommended for precision. - Use single keywords rather than long sentences to avoid distorted images. - Separate keywords with dots or spaces; spaces increase keyword count. - After entering keywords, click **Create** to generate stickers. - Creation progress and server link are displayed; queues may cause delays. - Minimize the window during waiting using the upper-right arrow button. - Upon completion, click **Apply** to add the sticker to the Object window and apply it. #### Additional Features - **Diverse Outputs:** Same prompts yield different sticker variations. - **True Icon:** Generates new images similar to the previous result while maintaining prompt characteristics. - **Random Button:** Generates stickers with random pattern types and keywords. --- ### Virtual Model Face Generator Developed in partnership with NOVA, this function modifies or creates close-up virtual model faces using AI or uploaded images, altering facial textures and grid structures for realistic results. - **Supported Virtual Models:** Current support primarily for female models; future versions will expand gender options. - **Integration:** Compatible with virtual models from the TuKu window and Connect platform. - **Face Generation Options:** - AI-based generation using gender, age, and race presets with keyword prompts. - Upload specific facial images for direct conversion. #### Activation Methods 1. **Menu Activation:** Virtual Model Human Generator under the Virtual Model menu. 2. **Attribute Editor Activation:** Select a virtual model, then access the tool from the Body Model box. #### Interface Details - **Top Tabs:** Choose between **Prompt** (AI generation) or **Picture** (image upload). - **Presets:** - Gender (auto-set based on model, currently female-only) - Age (10 to 80 years) - Race (Asian, Caucasian, African, Middle Eastern, Latin American) - **Keyword Prompt:** Input descriptive facial features. - **History Record:** Shows previous creations and used prompt keywords; resets when software closes. - **Image Upload:** Upload specific face images for conversion; history also retained until software closes. #### Operation Process - Select age, race, gender. - Enter keywords in the prompt box (English preferred). - Click **Start** to generate the face. - Preview AI-generated faces shown in the interface. - After generation, click **Switch** to apply the new face to the virtual model. - The model’s body texture and color automatically adjust to match the face tone. #### Additional Features - **Random Icon:** Inserts random facial feature hints to inspire varied results. - **True Icon:** Generates new images similar to previous ones while allowing prompt modifications. - **Queue Management:** Users can perform other tasks while waiting; window can be minimized. - **Input Tips:** - Use single words over long sentences. - Separate keywords using two numbers (likely meaning separators). - Enclose words in square brackets to emphasize them. #### Image Upload Conversion - Ensure virtual model gender matches the uploaded image. - High-quality images should clearly show facial features without hair or shadows. - After uploading, click **Convert** to apply changes. - Body textures and colors adjust for natural coordination. #### Summary This function simplifies and speeds up the creation of realistic and diverse virtual model faces. It is currently a public version, with potential policy changes in the future. --- ## 2D Floating Version Functions This section details improvements in 2D CAD editing, panel selection, measurement tools, seam allowance, and paper pattern handling aimed at enhancing workflow efficiency and precision. ### 2D CAD Continuous Editing Optimization Improves workflow by simplifying linked panel line management: - **Display Link Option:** Located in the 2D panel window menu bar, it toggles visibility of linked line diagrams. - **Link Removal:** After selecting the Edit Panel tool, linked lines can be right-clicked and unlinked directly, streamlining previous multi-step processes. - **Linked Line Adjustment:** - Adjusting length or proportion of a linked line now modifies all linked counterparts accordingly. - Moving or rotating linked lines maintains length relationships. - **Array Tool:** Selecting both ends of a linked line allows simultaneous endpoint modification via the Array tool. ### 2D Panel Selection Efficiency Improvement Enhances selection flexibility for inner lines and panels: - Use **Edit Panel** tool. - Hold **CTRL** and left-click/drag to select multiple inner lines or panels within a dragged area. - Simplifies selection of multiple components, especially in complex designs like skirt folds. ### 2D Edit Panel Measurement Angle Introduces angle measurement on panel outlines or overlapping lines: - Select panel endpoints with the Edit Panel tool. - Right-click and choose the endpoint option to display the angle. - Angles dynamically update as lines move, assisting precise shaping. - Useful for checking and adjusting angles in pockets or special panel junctions. ### Seam Allowance Optimization Enhances seam allowance accuracy and flexibility: - **Panel Corner Seam Allowance:** - Previously caused repeated seam allowances at corner extensions, causing inaccuracies. - New Cut Position menu lets users choose between Extension Point (cut to vertical extension) or Center Position (previous behavior). - **Seam Allowance for Hollows:** - Hollow areas inside panels are now recognized as outlines. - Seam allowance can be added inside hollows using the Seam Allowance tool. ### 2D Paper Pattern Improvement Improves DXF import positioning: - Previously, paper patterns far from the center imported without repositioning. - Now, DXF imports are centered at the 00 position in the 2D window. - Maintains all paper sample layers, improving workflow and sample management. ### Code Selection Improvement Optimizes code display and color management in the Object window: - Code lines display colors randomly by default. - Eye icon toggles visibility of code lines by size. - Color blocks can be clicked to remove or modify colors. - Creating new code sizes auto-generates random colors which can be customized. - Enables clearer identification and management of paper samples and codes. --- ## New Hair Function and Material Updates This section introduces new hair-related material options and rendering support aimed at enhancing hair realism. ### Hair Material and Lighting Compensation - Added hair material to the **Composite Energy** compensation light option. - Addresses high-density hair rendering issues where light does not penetrate well, causing darker appearances. - Enabling this option restores lost light, making hair brightness more realistic. ### V-Ray Rendering Support for Hair - Hair effects are viewable only within the V-Ray rendering window. - Hair parameters include: length, thickness, density, curl, gravity, curve strength, curve direction, and initial direction. - Eight distinct hair patterns can be applied. ### Hair Pattern Stickers - **Curl Pattern:** Black-and-white pattern controlling curl quantity and radius. Black=no curl, white=curl. - **Gravity Pattern:** Simulates hair gravity using a black-and-white pattern. - **Curve Intensity Sticker:** Black-and-white; black=no curve, white=curve intensity. - **Curve Direction Sticker:** RGB color pattern defining hair curve direction by color. - **Initial Direction Sticker:** Defines hair root direction. These stickers can be applied in Substance Painter and imported into CLO for enhanced hair realism. --- ## Rendering Updates and Optimizations This section covers new rendering capabilities, camera options, and image quality improvements. ### 360-Degree Panoramic Landscape Rendering - Supports rendering of full 360-degree panoramic images. - Enables creation of virtual exhibition halls inside CLOSET. - Workflow: - Import OBJ files into CLO. - Position them at the center of the 360-degree space. - Create wall-mounted exhibition halls on all four sides. - Result is a natural panoramic environment suitable for virtual exhibitions. ### Camera Lens Type Options - New **Lens Type** option in the camera attribute window. - Two choices: - **Default:** Existing lens with 15° field of view. - **Full Lens:** New option with
